answer: Call it a sponsor sieve: vault is the one roll binding key, route and first verdict, so every cipher, one fake identity, collides there. The kth cipher enters only when k sponsors from unrelated clusters each lock (k−1)^2 ivory to that key; a sponsor backs one live cipher, and matching outputs slash both lots. Since live count is updated serially, n cipher need n(n+1)/2 unrelated sponsors and about n^4/4 ivory. It breaks if vault merges aliases, clusters are captured, or ivory moves.
